reasons: Both give a sound upper/lower 4-day plan with pattern-preserving substitutes, McGill-style core work, RPE-based double progression, a 24-hour pain rule and red flags. A explicitly refuses to derive loads from the old maxes and starts with 2 sets at RPE 6, while B says its starting weights were estimated from the 120/150 kg lifts and suggests a heavier leg press start (100-140 kg), which fits the conservative-start criterion less well. B gains some ground by putting the full McGill Big 3 in every warm-up and building a deload into week 4, but A's deload after week 4 and its trap-bar ceiling are still adequate, so A wins narrowly.
